item.title: 【AI4S】 Filter By:
item.description: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. item.description: Emergency department disposition decisions integrate measurements, narratives and contextual risk. We developed SMARTriage AI, a multi-agent system combining role-specialized language-model agents with deterministic rules, intended as safety gates, to recommend admission or discharge. In a retrospective, single-center development study of 469 valid-label adult internal medicine and geriatric encounters from one 24-h period (468 analyzed; 154 admitted), prompts and rules were refined over about 30 cycles on the same cohort, without a held-out set. Apparent accuracy was 88.2% (95% CI, 85.0–90.9%) and admission recall 96.1%. Accuracy was 97.2% with physician summary or recommendations text (n = 248) and 78.2% without it (n = 220); with the text withheld it was 65.0%. After peer review, a redesigned system (v2), evaluated on all 469 encounters under a protocol locked before the runs, discriminated worse than a single language-model agent (Setting A AUC 0.794 vs. 0.821–0.823). At the pre-specified thresholds, accuracy was 76.3% for v2 versus 67.0% for discharging everyone.
